page: Amazon Web Services c7i.metal-48xl is a bare-metal, compute-optimized server instance built on the x86_64 architecture. It features a dedicated 96-core Intel Xeon 8488C processor operating at 3.2 GHz, supporting 192 virtual CPUs with two threads per core. Hardware acceleration capability is expanded via Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), AVX-512, and specialized cryptographic instruction sets. The system includes 384.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 5 GHz, providing a ratio of 2.0 GB of memory per core. The instance contains zero GPUs and no bundled local NVMe storage, while network connectivity is delivered via a 50 Gbps baseline interface.

Benchmark measurements show top-tier multi-core performance, evidenced by a multi-core stress-ng score of 171174.13 and a PassMark CPU score of 125745.92. Cache-intensive execution is supported by a 105 MB L3 cache, contributing to large-block uncached memory read bandwidth of 423.72 GB/sec. Software compilation and ray tracing tests demonstrate top-tier execution times. In contrast, single-core processing yields average-to-strong results, with a single-core stress-ng rating of 2069.29 and a single-core Geekbench score of 2101.0. High-concurrency network tasks achieve top-tier throughput, including Redis SET performance reaching 191.08 million operations per second.

The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM configuration concentrates resources on parallel processing capacity rather than large per-core memory capacity. The absence of local disk drives requires external network storage attached across the 50 Gbps fabric. Cost efficiency is driven by high resource density, maximizing throughput for parallelized compute tasks without GPU overhead. Primary workload fits include high-concurrency web serving, large-scale software compilation, in-memory caching platforms, CPU-based machine learning inference, and multithreaded data processing pipelines.
